title: BisChIP-Seq/ChIP-BS-Seq
scope: Illumina shared explanatory schematic of BisChIP-seq/ChIP-BS-seq, with ChIP-BMS retained as a catalogue alias and implementation applicability qualified below. Image inventory: leftmost explanatory title cartoon; input "DNA-protein complex with methylated histones and methylated DNA"; arrow to "Sonicate" with separate complexes; arrow to "Immunoprecipitate" with pink antibodies and a faded nonselected complex; "Purify DNA and shear" producing naked DNA; a fanned sequence enlargement under "Bisulfite conversion" showing successive bisulfite and PCR states; arrow to a final blue DNA line with the visible right-edge label "DNA". The fanned inset is a chemical-state explanation, not three sample branches. Antibodies and modification dots are contextual reagents/symbols, without a chemical end-group legend. End-repair/methylated-adapter ligation and NGS are explicitly text-supported interfaces, not extra depicted panels. The main graph preserves the full shared drawing; method_scopes separates that depiction from primary-verified operation assignments. Routine execution details and unshown size-selection branches of individual experiments are outside this explanatory scope.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate

operations.label: End-repair and methylated-adapter ligation (text-supported interface)
operations.description: Prepares captured DNA for sequencing and attaches bisulfite-protected adapters before conversion. This single broad block bridges purified DNA to the converted library; it is supplied by the card and primary text and is not a separately depicted panel.
operations.mechanism: End-repair and adapter ligation are explicitly reported. In the verified ChIP-BS-seq implementation the adapter cytosines are 5-methylcytosines, preventing their deamination during conversion.
operations.information_effect: Adds the sequencing-library interface while retaining captured genomic DNA as the biological insert.

operations.label: Bisulfite conversion
operations.description: Acts on the adapter-bearing captured DNA. In the depicted sequence example the unmarked C becomes U while the marked C remains C; the protected adapters are supplied by the text-supported implementation.
operations.mechanism: The figure explicitly depicts the differential response of the illustrated cytosines to bisulfite; it supplies no further base-chemistry structures.
operations.information_effect: Converts an original methylation-state difference into a template-base difference that PCR can preserve in sequence.

operations.label: PCR

unknowns.question: Does "Purify DNA and shear" intentionally specify an additional post-ChIP fragmentation in each named implementation, and by what mechanism? The drawing explicitly retains that label, while Brinkman [b00047] begins library construction with already obtained ChIP DNA and does not specify that extra fragmentation. A variant-specific primary preparation description or original figure explanation would be needed to assign this extra shearing to a particular protocol.

Which full primary protocol independently defines ChIP-BMS, and which exact BisChIP-seq library steps correspond to the GR application? The catalogue supplies an alias assertion and the Jin abstract supplies an application, but neither verifies identical adapter chemistry or every depicted operation for these names. Full method text identifying the named implementations would resolve this.

What chemical specificity can be assigned to an unconverted C beyond the schematic marked-versus-unmarked cytosine example? The supplied figure and inspected primary passages do not establish chemical discrimination among all potentially bisulfite-resistant bases. A primary validation or chemical-specific assay description is needed for a stronger specificity claim; the captured-DNA architecture and illustrated C/T readout remain interpretable.
